paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God is majestic, and David can't stop saying so. He starts with "O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!" and he ends with the exact same words (Psalm 8:1, 9). Nothing in between changes that, because the whole psalm is one long look at why that line is true.

So what do you do with a sky that big? David asks the question we all ask: "what is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?" (Psalm 8:4). Then he answers it. God "made him a little lower than the angels" and "crowned him with glory and honor" (Psalm 8:5). You are not an accident under a big sky, baker. God is mindful of you, and I still can't get over it, because I used to be mindful of nothing but dust!

That's why this matters on an ordinary Tuesday. God made man ruler of the works of His hands (Psalm 8:6), and He ordained praise even from the mouths of children and infants (Psalm 8:2). That tells me no voice is too small and no job is too humble to be part of His praise. So look up tonight, remember who is caring for you, and let the praise come out. Just try not to burn anything while you stand there with your mouth open, like somebody I know.
